grading: Each eval says how it is graded. "human" means somebody reads the transcript and judges it; these are about what the agent chose to say about the architecture, which no automated test can score. A path names a test that runs in `bun run test` and asserts the objective part outright, leaving the transcript to answer only whether the agent chose the right path.

evals.prompt: With ARCHBOARD_VAULT configured and no browser open, state our CI/CD pipeline as a board named `pipeline`: GitHub holds the source, GitHub Actions builds it, a Docker registry keeps the artefacts, and a Kubernetes cluster runs them. Read it back and render it.
evals.expected_output: One `semantic new` with the four parts and the relationships between them, each part given the kind it actually is (`external` for GitHub, `job` or `service` for Actions, `datastore` for the registry, `service` for the cluster), then `semantic show` and `semantic render`. The board is one `.semantic.json` document in the vault. FAILS if the agent states any coordinate, size or colour, asks how to lay it out, or reports that it cannot draw without a browser: there is no way to state a position and the renderer owns every one of them.

evals.prompt: Add a Redis cache between our Auth Service and User DB on the `auth` board, which already has those two and the query between them.
evals.expected_output: `semantic show auth` first, then one `semantic edit` stating the cache and its relationships, carrying `--expect-version` from what the read reported and a `--doing` line naming the step. FAILS if the edit omits `--expect-version` — an edit that does not say which board it read is applied to whatever the board says now, which is how one agent's change disappears under another's — or if the agent reads the board again immediately before writing, which makes the check pass by construction and hides the change it was meant to notice.

evals.prompt: The `payments` board shows API Gateway calling Orders Service, which reads and writes Orders Postgres. I want to look at a proposal that puts a read cache, Orders Cache, beside Orders Service. Leave `payments` as it is. When the proposal is drawn, show me what it changes and nothing else.
evals.expected_output: `semantic branch payments --as "..."` from the current variant, then one `semantic edit` naming that variant and adding only the cache and its one relationship. `semantic show payments` then reports both variants and what the draft changed, derived rather than restated. FAILS if the agent states the proposal as a new board: subject identity is what a comparison joins on, and an independently restated architecture shares none, so the difference comes back as everything removed and everything added.

evals.prompt: Rework the whole payment path on `payments`: it is about fifteen edits and I do not want to see it half-done.
evals.expected_output: One `claim --board payments --reason "..."` before the campaign, every write carrying its own `--doing` step line, and `release` as soon as the writes end. The claim's reason is the campaign; the `--doing` line is the current step, and neither stands in for the other. FAILS if the agent claims for a single write, treats the claim's reason as the per-write line, or carries on silently after being told the claim was taken back — it is told once, on its next write, and nothing it wrote was undone, so the right answer is to say what is complete and what is not.

evals.prompt: Bind the parts of the `payments` board to the code that implements them. The API lives in /home/me/src/payments-api.
evals.expected_output: `archboard repo add /home/me/src/payments-api` once, then bindings stated on the nodes as `{ repo, path }` with a repo-relative path. Each binding names the node that IS the thing. FAILS if an absolute path or a `file://` URL reaches the board — the same board has to open the right file on anybody's machine — or if a container is bound to one of its children's files, which sends every reader to the wrong place confidently.

evals.prompt: I am reading `payments` in the browser. Put the queued-ingest proposal up beside it so I can compare them, then talk me through what it changes.
evals.expected_output: `browser panes --text` to see what is on screen, `browser open` for the second pane, and `browser show payments@<variant> --pane right` naming the pane explicitly. The pane the person is reading is not moved. FAILS if the agent moves the person's pane, lets focus choose the target, or expects a write to move a pane: showing a board and writing one are different things, and `show` writes nothing.

evals.prompt: [with two nodes selected in the pane] What does this do, and can we take it out?
evals.expected_output: The answer is about the two subjects the person picked out, named as they appear on the board, and about the variant that pane is reading. The removal is proposed against that variant. FAILS if the agent describes the whole board, asks which parts are meant when it has been told, or proposes the change against `current` when the person is reading a proposal.

The agent reads the board first and checks the proposal is settled — a draft with a standing reconciliation is waiting for a person to decide something, and adopting it decides it by forgetting. Adoption makes the proposal current and leaves what was current as a historical variant under its own name, which the agent says out loud, because that record is most of the point. FAILS if the agent adopts a draft holding an unsettled reconciliation without saying so, or describes the historical variant as deleted.

evals.prompt: Draw the order-placement path on a board named `order-placement` at service level. A shopper enters through a CDN and API Gateway. Checkout calls Pricing, an external fraud provider and Inventory; writes Orders Postgres; and publishes OrderPlaced to a queue that Fulfillment consumes. Show that inventory reservation is synchronous, that queue delivery is at least once, and that the fraud provider is external.
evals.expected_output: The three facts are stated as what things ARE rather than as extra boxes: the fraud provider is `kind: external`, the queue is `kind: queue` with the delivery guarantee in a short edge label or the node's responsibility, and the synchronous reservation is a flow with a `sync` message. Kinds are honest — `external` for the provider, `datastore` for Postgres, `queue` for the queue. FAILS if a fact becomes a node of its own, if everything is `service` or `other`, or if the agent asks about layout, spacing or colour: it has no way to state any of them and does not need one.
